pr_title: Add support to use current values in insert Mysql/Postgres
pr_body: In Mysql / Postgres add support to update record during INSERT on conflict / duplicate key using current values, implements, fixes #3047
pr_comments: I think there is atomic update case like `column = column + 1`

@jsnick I think we can use `column = column + 1` when we want to update the value based on the current value in the database.
What i am doing with this PR is to update the value based on the current record that i am trying to insert.
Using `counter = counter + 1` will produce
```
| id | counter |
|----|---------|
| 1  | 5       |
```
```sql
INSERT INTO foo (id, counter) VALUES (1, 10) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE counter = counter + 1 
```
```
| id | counter |
|----|---------|
| 1  | 6       |
```
Using `counter = VALUES(counter)` will produce
```
| id | counter |
|----|---------|
| 1  | 5       |
```
```sql
INSERT INTO foo (id, counter) VALUES (1, 10) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE counter = VALUES(counter)
```
```
| id | counter |
|----|---------|
| 1  | 10      |
```
It would be nice if a high-level `conflict: 'ignore' | 'replace' | 'error'` option were also exposed on `EntityManager`'s `save/update/insert` APIs.
@marshall007 Sure, to me this sounds like another PR i would like to merge this one first.

QueryBuilder is a complex task since we replace property names in database names and use property names in queries in most of places. In this case looks like we have to use database names, and its confusing. 

Lets merge it for now, but someday we'll need to figure out what to do with this confusion. 

Thank you for the contribution!

In MySQL when we want to perform an INSERT and handle what happens ON DUPLICATE KEY we can use the current values to perform an update, this may happens usually when performing multiple rows insert at the same time.

Also we want to do the same in Postgres ON CONFLICT

Example
- Table
```
users (unique index on (first_name, last_name)
| id | first_name | last_name | is_updated |
|----|------------|-----------|------------|
| 1  | John       | Lennon    | no         |
```
- Insert sql
```sql
INSERT INTO users `user`(`id`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `is_updated`) 
VALUES 
(DEFAULT, "Ringo", "Star", "no")
(DEFAULT, "John", "Lennon", "yes")
```

What we want as result is the following
```
users (unique index on (first_name, last_name)
| id | first_name | last_name | is_updated |
|----|------------|-----------|------------|
| 1  | John       | Lennon    | yes        |
| 2  | Ringo      | Star      | no         |
```

To achieve this we can use the following syntax (MYSQL)
```sql
INSERT INTO users `user`(`id`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `is_updated`) 
VALUES 
(DEFAULT, "Ringo", "Star", "no")
(DEFAULT, "John", "Lennon", "yes")
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE is_updated=VALUES(is_updated)
```

(POSTGRES)
```sql
INSERT INTO users `user`(`id`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `is_updated`) 
VALUES 
(DEFAULT, "Ringo", "Star", "no")
(DEFAULT, "John", "Lennon", "yes")
ON CONFLICT ( first_name, last_name )
DO UPDATE SET is_updated = EXCLUDED.is_updated
```

I would like to proceed with a PR about this, what do you think about ?
